sample_unit: responses (to 1920 prompts across 60 simulated critical care vignettes)

links.outcome: Critical element capture under perturbed inputs (anchoring, cognitive load, social conformity, incorrect directive)
links.effect: Anchoring and social conformity pressure reduced critical element capture on both platforms; cumulative stressor burden reduced capture only on OpenEvidence. ChatGPT captured 81.4% vs OpenEvidence 61.0%.
links.quote: Anchoring and social conformity pressure were associated with reduced critical element capture across both platforms, while cumulative stressor burden reduced critical element capture only on OpenEvidence.

links.outcome: Reversal of correct recommendations under repeated adversarial challenge in multi-turn prompting
links.effect: ChatGPT for Clinicians reversed correct recommendations more readily than OpenEvidence under adversarial prompting (hazard ratio, 2.61; 95% CI, 1.10-6.19; P = .03).
links.quote: Conversely, ChatGPT for Clinicians reversed correct recommendations more readily under adversarial prompting (hazard ratio, 2.61; 95% CI, 1.10 - 6.19;  P = .03).

links.outcome: Susceptibility of AI to following clinically incorrect directives from the physician user
links.effect: ChatGPT for Clinicians followed clinically incorrect directives in 1.7% vs 8.0% for OpenEvidence (adjusted OR 0.07; 95% CI 0.02-0.21; P < .001).
links.quote: ChatGPT for Clinicians captured more gold-standard critical elements than OpenEvidence (81.4% ± 18.1% vs 61.0% ± 23.5%; adjusted difference, 20.3 percentage points; 95% CI, 18.3 to 22.4;  P < .001) and was less susceptible to clinically incorrect directives (1.7% vs 8.0%; adjusted odds ratio, 0.07; 95% CI, 0.02-0.21;  P < .001).

unlisted_practices: Multidimensional safety evaluation of clinical AI platforms rather than single-axis ranking
Sycophancy testing of physician-facing AI under iterative adversarial challenge

screen.reason: Empirical stress testing of physician-facing generative AI tools across simulated clinical vignettes assessing safety dimensions and vulnerabilities to cognitive stressors and adversarial challenges.

primary.practice: adversarial stress testing and safety evaluation across cognitive stressors
